review.why: Design stable APIs and interfaces: contract first, consistent errors, validation at boundaries, additive changes and idempotency keys done right.
review.summary: Principles and patterns for REST APIs, module boundaries and TypeScript interfaces: Hyrum's Law, the one-version rule, contract-first design, one error shape, validation only at system edges, additive changes, predictable naming, and a detailed section on honouring idempotency keys. Ends with common rationalizations, red flags and a verification checklist.
strengths: Concrete and opinionated, with good and bad code side by side (status code mapping, validation at the boundary, discriminated unions, branded IDs).
The idempotency section covers the parts that lose money: atomic claim, payload hash, in-flight duplicates, unknown outcomes and retention.
Red flags and a verification checklist make it usable as a review tool.
cautions: Principles, not a framework recipe: no GraphQL schema design or OpenAPI tooling, and examples are TypeScript and Express style.
References other skills of the same repository (such as deprecation-and-migration) that a single-skill install does not include.
Read in full but not run here.
